proof_spans.label: the author's own proof environment immediately following the lemma: over the algebraic closure, the commutator morphism h: (x, y) -> (x, xyx^{-1}y^{-1}) is a morphism over the first projection, constant on the fibre e x A; the collapse lemma gives a neighbourhood U of e over which the fibres of h are finite, so for each x in U(k) the commutator endomorphism y -> xyx^{-1}y^{-1} of A has finite image; being a group homomorphism on the connected variety A, its image is connected and finite, hence the single point e; thus the commutator is trivial on U x A, and translating by U-points covers A(k), forcing the group law to be abelian (source lines 1873-1893)

core_obligations: Set-up (proof lines 1876-1884): over k-bar the commutator morphism h is a morphism over pr_0 and h|_{e x A} is constant (e, e).

Finiteness near e (proof lines 1884-1888): 0AH8 yields U around e with h|_{U x A} factoring through something finite over U, so each commutator endomorphism y -> xyx^{-1}y^{-1} takes finitely many values.

Triviality (proof lines 1888-1893): the commutator endomorphism is a group homomorphism of the connected variety A, so its image is connected and finite, hence {e}; the commutator is trivial on U x A, and since every k-point is a translate of a point of U the group law is abelian.
proof_roadmap: Reduce to the algebraic closure and set up the commutator morphism (proof lines 1876-1884).
Get finiteness of the commutator image over a neighbourhood of e (proof lines 1884-1888).
Conclude the image is trivial and commute the group law (proof lines 1888-1893).
